notes: Reconciliation-only -- schema/enum/referential integrity for the underlying raw tables are already covered by context/validations/lifecycle_raw.json.

Executed by src/validate_loan_portfolio.py, which independently recomputes every metric in pandas from raw Parquet (never importing src/etl_spark_loan_portfolio.py's Spark logic) and compares against the curated summary it wrote.

total_outstanding_principal_status_vocabulary_drift is a bound check (src.lifecycle_validation_helpers.bound_check), not a reconciliation -- it compares the curated value against a payment_status-label-agnostic recomputation (amount field only), which stays correct even if the payment_status vocabulary is renamed upstream. See src.validate_loan_portfolio._amount_agnostic_outstanding_principal.

rules.description: curated loan_portfolio.loan_count must match the number of raw loans records.
curated loan_portfolio.active_loan_count must match the count of raw loans with loan_status == ACTIVE.
curated loan_portfolio.closed_loan_count must match the count of raw loans with loan_status == CLOSED.
curated loan_portfolio.defaulted_loan_count must match the count of raw loans with loan_status == DEFAULTED.
curated loan_portfolio.total_funded_principal must match the sum of principal_amount across raw loans.
curated loan_portfolio.total_outstanding_principal must match, per loan, principal_amount minus net successful payment_events amount (PAID net of any REVERSED), floored at 0, summed across all loans.
curated loan_portfolio.avg_interest_rate must match the mean interest_rate across raw loans.

curated loan_portfolio.total_accrued_interest must match, per ACTIVE loan (business_rules.interest_accrual.accrues_on_statuses), principal_amount * interest_rate * (days since originated_at) / 365, summed.

The gap between curated total_outstanding_principal (business_rules.successful_payment_statuses-driven) and a payment_status-label-agnostic recomputation (amount field only) must not exceed 30% of total_funded_principal -- a wider gap means the approved successful-payment vocabulary no longer matches what the data actually contains (e.g. an upstream contract rename like PAID -> SETTLED), not just the expected LATE-payment exclusion.
